_about: Per-region bone settings for the fracture engine. All values are data; change them here, not in code.

cortex._note: MODELLED cortex (owner's decision). Thickness in mm against position along the bone (0 = proximal end, 1 = distal end), straight lines between points. Same peak and end values as the owner's earlier Tibia Fracture Lab.

sources.claim: Cortex is thickest toward the mid-diaphysis
sources.ref: Capozza RF et al. J Anat 2010;216:470-81

sources.claim: Anterior cortex is thicker than posterior; medial and lateral do not differ
sources.ref: Maeda K et al. J Exp Orthop 2020;7:78

sources.claim: Medullary diameter 13-32 mm between 20 and 80 % of tibial length (used as a check of the model)
sources.ref: Taylor CE et al. Anat Rec 2020;303:2847-56

cortex._note: MODELLED cortex. Same values as the owner's earlier Tibia Fracture Lab. No published source found for these numbers.

default_profile._note: Owner's decision 18 Nov 2026: neck and trochanteric fractures start as elderly bone; the page can switch.

young._note: MODELLED cortex (owner's decision). Thickness in mm against position along the femur (0 = proximal end, 1 = distal end), straight lines between points. No published ABSOLUTE thickness values were found in the sources checked; the young-to-elderly difference and the thin superolateral neck follow the sources. 'boosts' thicken the cortex towards one side (0 anterior, 90 medial, 180 posterior): posterior = linea aspera, medial at the lesser trochanter level = calcar region (no source for the amount).

sources.claim: Older femoral cortex is up to 1.5 mm thinner anteriorly and 2 mm thinner posteriorly than young (<40 y) bone; the isthmus is more distal in the elderly (CT, 919 femora)
The superolateral femoral neck cortex is thin and thins with age (women 6.4 % per decade)
Femoral canal isthmus: mean diameter 10.49 +/- 1.52 mm, at 55 +/- 4.8 % of femoral height (3D CT, 204 femora); used as a CHECK of the modelled canal (young model 12 mm, elderly 16 mm)
sources.ref: Su XY et al. Biomed Res Int 2015:459612

elderly._note: MODELLED cortex (owner's decision). Thickness in mm against position along the femur (0 = proximal end, 1 = distal end), straight lines between points. No published ABSOLUTE thickness values were found in the sources checked; the young-to-elderly difference and the thin superolateral neck follow the sources. 'boosts' thicken the cortex towards one side (0 anterior, 90 medial, 180 posterior): posterior = linea aspera, medial at the lesser trochanter level = calcar region (no source for the amount). Elderly: about 1.5-2 mm thinner in the shaft, peak moved distally, 0.8 mm at the neck.

cortex._note: MODELLED cortex. Thin shell all round (the patella is mostly cancellous bone). No published thickness value was found; no medullary canal.
